E2E-75.when: the harness drives pending, sealed, finalized, syncing, reconnecting, behind, rebuilding, rewound, and blocked states
E2E-75.then: each SHALL have a stable locator, persistent text, non-color-only semantics, correct command gating, and an assistive-technology announcement

fiveObligationsDecomposed.stableLocator: a locator that does not depend on the message wording. Shipped: data-testid="tactical-lifecycle-state" plus data-state=<state> (src/components/multiplayer/TacticalLifecycleStateBanner.tsx:31-32). The row asserts getByTestId(...).getAttribute('data-state') equals the driven state name.
fiveObligationsDecomposed.persistentText: the banner renders on EVERY posture including `live`, not only on trouble (src/lib/lifecycle/lifecycleState.ts:19-25 says so explicitly). The row asserts the element is visible and its textContent is non-empty in every driven state, and that the text is the state's own MESSAGES entry (src/lib/multiplayer/tacticalLifecycleState.ts:132-143) rather than a shared string.
fiveObligationsDecomposed.nonColorOnlySemantics: colour alone must not carry the state. This is the obligation with real teeth: LIFECYCLE_TONE (src/lib/lifecycle/lifecycleState.ts:60-71) gives `behind`, `rewound` and `rebuilding` the IDENTICAL palette triple 'border-sky-700 bg-sky-900/30 text-sky-200', and `pending`/`syncing`/`reconnecting` share 'border-amber-700 bg-amber-900/30 text-amber-200'. Three states are colour-indistinguishable from each other and another three likewise. The non-colour signal is therefore the MESSAGE TEXT plus data-state. The row asserts the rendered text differs pairwise across every driven state - i.e. the set of texts has the same cardinality as the set of driven states - which is a property a tone-only banner cannot satisfy.
fiveObligationsDecomposed.correctCommandGating: commandsEnabled is true for exactly `live` and `finalized` (src/lib/multiplayer/tacticalLifecycleState.ts:155). The row asserts the action bar's intent controls are operable in `finalized` and NOT operable in the seven degraded states, read through the shipped commandGate prop path (src/components/multiplayer/NetworkedGameSurface.tsx:392-397) rather than by clicking a disabled button - clicking a disabled control is a no-op either way and proves nothing (the discipline gmRewindPreviewPhrasing.ts:22-26 already names).
fiveObligationsDecomposed.assistiveTechnologyAnnouncement: the banner is role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true" (TacticalLifecycleStateBanner.tsx:34-39). Assertion method: Playwright role/name queries - page.getByRole('status') resolves the banner, and its accessible NAME is its text content (no aria-label, no aria-labelledby), so `expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: MESSAGES[state] }))` is the announcement assertion. An accessibility snapshot (page.accessibility.snapshot()) is captured per state as EVIDENCE in the run directory, but the GATE is the role/name query - a snapshot diff would gate on sibling chrome the unit does not own.

E2E-77.then: the UI SHALL identify the actor-safe conflict class, base revision or branch, and recovery action without leaking private data

threeObligationsDecomposed.actorSafeConflictClass: the surface must name WHICH class refused, in words an actor can act on. Shipped surfaces: (a) src/components/multiplayer/NetworkedGameSurface.overlays.tsx:230-253 IntentErrorToast, data-testid="intent-error-toast", role="alert", text 'Action rejected (<CODE>): <reason>'; (b) the lifecycle banner's `blocked` posture message (tacticalLifecycleState.ts:139). The row asserts the discriminator is present and specific, and records as a NON-CLAIM that no reachable class carries a numeric base revision today.
threeObligationsDecomposed.recoveryActionWithoutLeak: the recovery action is rendered VERBATIM from the server and never paraphrased: src/components/multiplayer/NetworkedGameSurface.branchRecovery.tsx:8-21, data-testid="tactical-branch-recovery-action". The 'without leaking private data' clause is implemented as a deliberate DROP of operator detail - gmRewindPreviewPhrasing.ts:10-15 ('THE `detail` FIELD IS NEVER SHOWN' - it names branch ids, outcome ids and revisions) and ServerMatchHostBranchAdmission.ts:205-207 ('the lease id, owner and fencing epoch are authority facts ... naming a rebuild's owner to a player is a disclosure this refusal does not need to make'). The row asserts the SAFETY property directly: the rendered conflict text does not contain the peer's playerId, the peer's wire token, the lease id, or any branch id the actor was not already shown - the same 'assert at the safety property, not at a proxy for it' discipline U1b's M4 mutant forced (tasks.md:588).

projectionRebuildReachability.claim: No in-paths lever puts a match or campaign stream into PROJECTION_REBUILDING, so neither the `rebuilding` lifecycle state nor the `rebuild` conflict class can be driven from e2e/ or scripts/qc alone.
chain: The tactical refusal is refuseDuringHistoryRebuild (src/lib/multiplayer/server/ServerMatchHostBranchAdmission.ts:220-244). It is a pure read: `rebuilding = ctx.store.readMatchStreamRebuild(matchId)`; null means no refusal (:236).

readDurableStreamRebuild (src/lib/events/journal/EventHistoryDurableRebuild.ts:45-59) reads the branch + correction-lease tables in DATABASE_PATH (./data/mekstation.db, migrations 23-24 per the header at :12-18) and answers null when the SQLite service is uninitialized (:47).

So a refusal requires a LIVE CORRECTION LEASE ROW. Every acquireCorrectionLease call site in the tree: src/lib/multiplayer/server/history/GmCombatRewindCommit.ts:145, src/lib/multiplayer/server/ServerMatchHostRewindRebuild.ts:231, src/lib/multiplayer/server/history/CoordinatedOutcomeCorrectionTarget.steps.ts:174, src/lib/campaign/rebuild/CampaignRetroactiveCorrectionCommit.ts:175.

The only one behind an HTTP route is GmCombatRewindCommit, served by src/pages/api/matches/[id]/rewind-commit.ts - and that route is the @until-journal-cutover lane which answers 404 no-authoritative-history because the combat stream is never journaled (e2e/gm-two-player-rewind.pack.spec.ts:3-6).

CampaignRetroactiveCorrectionCommit has NO api route (find over src/pages/api and src/app/api for *correct*/*rewind* returns only campaigns/[id]/rewind-preview.ts, matches/[id]/rewind-preview.ts, matches/[id]/rewind-commit.ts; the two preview routes write nothing and take no lease).

decisionNeeded.recommendation: U1c = E2E-75 (seven drivable states + the live control). U1d = E2E-77 (three reachable classes). Run them sequentially, not in parallel.
reasons: The combined estimate is 642-770 non-generated lines against a 500-line cap. The cap is exceeded by the smaller of the two scenarios' whole budget, so trimming cannot save the combined shape.

The two scenarios share three files (the qc core, the qc pin suite, tasks.md). Splitting keeps each unit's diff reviewable, but it also means the two units cannot be in flight together - the holders rule forbids two in-flight units owning one path.

The two scenarios have different risk profiles. E2E-75 is a pure UI-observation pack over levers that already exist. E2E-77 has one arm (stale revision) whose reachability is PROBABLE but unproven, and carries the leak-safety assertion that U1b's M4 mutant showed is the easiest thing in this repo to fake. Bundling them would let the weaker arm hold the stronger one hostage.
Splitting isolates the owner gate: the rebuild pair blocks one obligation in each scenario, and a split lets the parent rule once and have the ruling apply cleanly to two narrower behavior sentences.

drop stale revision and claim two classes
